clue.text: Writing on the wall — it may be all up for you!

definitions.text: Writing on the wall — it may be all up for you!

parts.words: Writing on the wall — it may be all up for you!
parts.note: not the biblical omen of doom but a literal wall bearing written items, every one of them pinned up for passers-by to read

explanation.surface: A grim warning that the game is up for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing on the wall' is an idiom for a sign of coming doom, and 'all up for you' seems to confirm it; read literally, it is notices pinned up on a wall for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A board fixed to a wall where written announcements are displayed for general reading.

clue.text: Although in flight, all passengers must be seated!

definitions.meaning: despite this, even so: a conjunction meaning in spite of

definitions.text: in flight, all passengers must be seated!
definitions.meaning: split into three words, nobody upright: none of the passengers on their feet

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a formal equivalent of despite or even so, while split it describes passengers who are sitting.

clue.text: To do it well takes time with every individual

definitions.text: To do it well takes time with every individual

parts.note: every individual means each

explanation.surface: Good instruction needs time spent with each pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Good instruction of pupils needs time given to each learner, which is what teaching well involves.

clue.text: Unite associate with a Tory

parts.note: a Tory is a Conservative, shortened to Con
to associate with is to join

explanation.surface: Someone urges a merger with a Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To conjoin is to bring together or combine, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Sale reported as fantastic

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so we want the word that sounds like the sale

parts.note: a bazaar is a sale of goods, often for charity

explanation.surface: A sale is described in the press as terrific.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bizarre is weird, strange, outlandish in the way something fantastic can be.

clue.text: Case viable at issue

indicators.note: issue as in come out or emerge, the letters of viable at emerging in a new form

explanation.surface: A legal case that is workable is under dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at issue' looks like one phrase, but 'at' is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablative is a grammatical case in Latin, expressing means or separation.

clue.text: BP technical expert?

parts.note: BP the oil company suggests an engineer who teaches boring for oil, but a sergeant major is the parade-ground teacher of marching

explanation.surface: An engineer works for the oil company.
explanation.walkthrough: BP (British Petroleum) is a major oil company, which pushes towards oil-well boring; the answer is a military rank that trains recruits in marching drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned officer who trains soldiers in parade-ground drill, pictured as one teaching oil-well boring.

clue.text: State follows check on automobile — it means one might return with a new body

definitions.text: it means one might return with a new body

indicators.note: follows puts the State word after the other pieces

parts.note: to rein in is to check
a car is an automobile
a nation is a state

explanation.surface: A national traffic authority clamps down on car use.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebirth of the soul in a new physical form after death is the doctrine named here.

clue.text: Terror any one got tortured with questioning

indicators.note: tortured means twisted and distorted, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: In an interrogation, someone was tortured using terror.
explanation.definitionFit: An interrogatory remark or form asks something, so the adjective means asking.

clue.text: Get on board with endless internal unrest

indicators.note: unrest is disorder and agitation, telling us the letters before it are stirred into a new order
endless says the word internal loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone boards a vehicle amid turmoil within the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims INTERNAL to INTERNA, and 'unrest' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a railway carriage, the train-specific verb for getting aboard.

clue.text: Very many suffering in holy city

indicators.note: in places the suffering word inside the holy city's name

parts.note: Zion is the holy city, Jerusalem, in biblical usage
suffering means ill, unwell

explanation.surface: Countless people are in distress in Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for an indefinitely huge number, so it describes a great many.

clue.text: Be in rough condition and you need a Samaritan

indicators.note: to condition something is to treat or work it into a new state, here the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: When you are in a bad way you need someone charitable to help, or ring the Samaritans helpline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condition' looks like a noun after 'rough', but it is a verb working on BE IN ROUGH. The Good Samaritan parable answers the question 'who is my neighbour?'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the parable the Samaritan who helped the robbed traveller is held up as the true example of a neighbour.

clue.text: It's displayed on some letters until December

definitions.note: a placement phrase rather than a noun: the mark sits over certain letters

indicators.note: displayed means put on show, and the run of letters is on show across two clue words

explanation.surface: Something is put on show for a while, up to the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' simply links: the surface reads as a whole definition, but only 'on some letters' places the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the wavy diacritic placed over letters such as the Spanish n.

clue.text: Former men's tennis champion could be feminine?

definitions.meaning: Arthur ... won Wimbledon in 1975 and the US Open in 1968

explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe was an American who won the men's singles at Wimbledon, and the split A SHE denotes a female.

clue.text: Bury disabled archdeacon — he got in the way

parts.note: to bury a body is to inter it

indicators.note: dis-abled read literally: the word for an archdeacon has its able removed

parts.note: an archdeacon in the Church of England is styled the Venerable

explanation.surface: Someone thwarted an attempt to bury an archdeacon who was handicapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disabled' is read as dis-ABLE-d: VENERABLE without ABLE leaves VENER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who intervenes is a person who steps in and obstructs or interferes.

clue.text: Little openings in favour of the rising feminine soul

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: in Jung's psychology the anima is the feminine inner self of a man

explanation.surface: Someone supports the rising spirit of femininity.
explanation.definitionFit: Foramina are small holes or apertures in bone or tissue, the plural of foramen.

clue.text: Tide now in — a disaster across the country

indicators.note: a disaster leaves everything in ruin and disorder, so the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A flood tide surges inland, causing a national catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that extends throughout a whole nation covers every part of the land.

clue.text: Marry without nest built in classy area

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the marry word goes round the rest

parts.note: to marry is to wed

indicators.note: built means constructed, making the letters of nest into something new

explanation.surface: A couple wed without building a home in an upmarket district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. The West End is London's fashionable theatre and shopping district.
explanation.definitionFit: London's West End is its fashionable, upmarket district of theatres and shops.

clue.text: Fed up with drama — there's nothing to it, actually

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the word fed runs backwards

parts.note: an act is a piece of drama, a play's division
nothing is O, zero

explanation.surface: Someone tired of theatre says it's dull really.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED to DEF; 'there's' and 'to it' simply join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in fact or in reality, as opposed to by law.

clue.text: Weapons turned on quarry

indicators.note: turned round means the word for weapons is read backwards

parts.note: gats is slang for guns

explanation.surface: Hunters turn their guns on the animal being chased.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is the classic hunted animal, the prey pursued in a hunt.

clue.text: Heavyweight state in South Pacific

definitions.note: the clue gives a location rather than a noun: the country is found there

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight
GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A powerful nation sits among the islands of the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonga's king Taufa'ahau Tupou IV was famously the heaviest monarch, adding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is an island kingdom located among the Polynesian archipelagos of the southern Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: P-plum?

parts.note: the letter P is the musical mark for quiet playing and a plum is a fruit, so this is a quiet fruit

explanation.walkthrough: In music p (piano) is the quiet or gentle marking; a plum belongs to the fruit bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Berries and similar tender produce are grouped as gentle produce, and the clue pictures one fruit marked quietly.

clue.text: She's upset after priest gets saucy

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled letters behind the priest's abbreviation

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters of she are rearranged

parts.note: she, the 's simply links

explanation.surface: A woman is upset when the vicar makes cheeky remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link; 'saucy' in the sense of cheeky, not tasting of sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh in the sense of cheeky or impertinent, especially overfamiliar, matches saucy.

clue.text: Mouth gets round staple food, if included

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: included says one word goes inside the staple food

parts.note: rice is a staple food across much of the world

explanation.surface: Someone eats a plate of rice and other staples.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening in the body, and the mouth is the obvious example.

clue.text: Producer of English carrot, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Who first grew the English carrot?
explanation.definitionFit: One who makes or brings something into being is its maker.

clue.text: King George embodies elements of the random ancestor

indicators.note: embodies means holds within its body, so King George's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: elements of suggests the letters of the following words used as raw components in a new order

explanation.surface: A king embodies features of a randomly chosen forebear.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's mother is a direct forebear one generation removed from your parents.
